User Notice
Terracotta is a third-party open source free software. Please provide feedback on any issues you encounter through the relevant channels during use.

Terracotta uses P2P technology. After a successful connection, users in the room will connect directly to each other, and no third-party server will relay your traffic. The final multiplayer experience largely depends on the network conditions of the participants.
During the entire multiplayer process, you must strictly comply with all laws and regulations of your country and region.

Host Tutorial

Host Tutorial:
Guest Tutorial:
Open the Multiplayer page and turn on "Enable multiplayer", then read the notice and confirm. Both host and guests need this.
Allow notifications. Multiplayer status lives in the notification bar, and Android is far more likely to kill the process without it.
Turn the switch on BEFORE launching the game: it is read when the game starts, so changing it afterwards does nothing.

In your singleplayer world press Esc, choose "Open to LAN", note the port (25565 by default, write it down if you change it), then click "Start LAN world". Skip this and the host step stays stuck on scanning.
Tap the floating menu ball in game, then "Menu", then "Multiplayer menu". That entry only exists when "Enable multiplayer" is on.
Tap "I want to host". The first time it asks for VPN permission, which is required to create the virtual network adapter.
Status goes: scanning LAN world, then starting room, then room started. The scanning step waits until the world is really opened to LAN.
When the room starts you get an invite code shaped U/XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX. It is copied to the clipboard automatically; if not, tap "Copy invite code".
Send the invite code to your friends and have them pick "I want to join" in the multiplayer menu.
Do not leave the world while playing: leaving it closes the room. To close it on purpose press "Exit"; the invite code dies with the room.
Enable multiplayer on the Multiplayer page and confirm the notice first, then launch the game. Staying on the main menu is enough, no world needed.
Tap the floating menu ball, then "Menu", then "Multiplayer menu", then "I want to join".
The first time it asks for VPN permission; without it the connection never succeeds.

Paste the invite code from the host and confirm. Spaces, dashes and the U/ prefix are cleaned up automatically, and the field tells you which protocol the code belongs to (Terracotta, PCL CE, Scaffolding).
Wait for "joining room" to finish. It shows a success estimate based on both networks; that is only a hint, not the real result.
Only "joined room" means success. If it fails, retry as prompted instead of tapping repeatedly while it is still joining.
Go back to the game main menu, open Multiplayer, refresh the list and double-click the Terracotta lobby entry to join.
If the list stays empty, use "Copy alternate address" in the multiplayer menu and paste it into Multiplayer, then Direct Connection.
Failing to enter the world is almost always a version or mod mismatch: game version, loader and mods must match the host exactly.
Offline accounts work; the alternate-address route does not support offline accounts, so prefer the lobby list.
Works with other Scaffolding clients such as FCL, HMCL and PCL CE; your friends do not have to use this launcher.
Room closed usually means the host left the world or closed the room on purpose; ask them to reopen and send a new code.
When it fails, open the log from the multiplayer menu; to report it, use "Share multiplayer core log" on the Multiplayer page.
